story: Gary is dry-fitting speaker and light wiring in his garage, holding off on mounting anything until the board gives its sign-off. Across the way, Donna is checking her pickleball bag and packing a spare paddle and extra balls for Gary's practice later. Hal is watching Magnolia Loop through his binoculars, taking stock of Halloween decorations, ornament counts, and any cart modifications he can spot. Meanwhile, Rosa is going over this week's per-diem shifts and blocking off evenings for Halloween parade planning.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Dry-fit the speaker and light wiring inside the garage, nothing mounted until the board signs off
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Check the bag and pack a spare paddle and extra balls for Gary's practice
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan Magnolia Loop for Halloween decorations, ornament counts, and cart modifications
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Check this week's per-diem shifts and block off evenings for Halloween parade planning

gary.thought_process: I'm at the house, it's a sunny Monday morning, and I just soldered and bench-tested the speaker and light wiring last tick. I filed the Architectural Review application at tick 156 and want to keep the cart legal, so I won't mount anything visible from the street until they sign off. The cart's in the garage, so I can safely do more prep work on it. Nobody's around, so no one to talk to. Best use of this hour is tidying up the wiring and dry-fitting the speaker mount on the cart inside the garage, out of sight of the street.

parameters.content: Dry-fit the speaker and light wiring inside the garage, nothing mounted until the board signs off

donna.thought_process: I'm home alone on a sunny Monday morning, and Gary and I have a ladder match coming up. Last tick I checked the club calendar, so now I should follow through on the other half of my plan: grab the pickleball bag and make sure everything is packed, paddles, balls, and a spare for Gary since he's never played. Then I can head out to book or confirm court time within the two-hour limit and start moving us up the ladder past Pruitt-Kowalski.

parameters.content: Check the bag and pack a spare paddle and extra balls for Gary's practice

hal.thought_process: I queued up the binoculars last tick to scan the Loop for Halloween decorations, ornament counts, and cart modifications. The scan is the action I intended, and this morning is a good clear one for it. Gary's cart mods and Donna's flamingos are still in the notebook until I verify them. Flamingo count was holding at three, but Halloween week brings decorations, and L-02 caps ornaments at three visible from the street. A supply sergeant counts before he reports, so I'll glass the Loop first.

parameters.content: Scan Magnolia Loop for Halloween decorations, ornament counts, and cart modifications

rosa.thought_process: The dinner went well and everyone's on board for Halloween carts. It's Monday morning, I'm alone at home, and my last memory was penciling in my per-diem shifts around parade planning. The shift schedule is right here, so I should check it now and block out time for planning before the flyer's week of decorating gets away from me. No one's around to talk to, and I shouldn't repeat invitations already made.

parameters.content: Check this week's per-diem shifts and block off evenings for Halloween parade planning

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
